t: This is the West Footbridge at London Zoo, in the City of Westminster. It was designed by Sir Hugh Casson, an architect who also worked as an interior designer, artist, writer and broadcaster on twentieth-century design. Casson was director of architecture for the 1951 Festival of Britain, and from 1976 to 1984 he served as president of the Royal Academy. It's a small piece of engineering, but it carries the name of one of Britain's best-known postwar designers.
